Can you explain the main options in simple terms?

Absolutely, I can break it down simply.

Think of our site in a few big buckets:

Roses
These are our specialty and what most people come for.
Live plants in 1-gallon pots (not cut flowers).
All are “own-root,” which just means they are grown on their own roots for better long-term health.
You can choose by:
Type: shrub, climber, groundcover
Color: pink, red, yellow, etc.
Fragrance level
Perennials
Other flowering plants and shrubs that come back every year.
Examples: lavender, hydrangea, echinacea, hosta, salvia, and many more.
Good for filling in around roses and making a full garden, not just one plant.
Bulbs
Things you plant once in fall that pop up in spring.
Examples: tulips, daffodils, allium, iris, ranunculus.
Sold mainly October through December and shipped then.
Soil amendments & fertilizers
These help your plants grow better but are not plants themselves.
Soil amendments (improve soil): mint compost, worm castings, cow manure, living soil, bone meal.
Fertilizers (feed the plant): OmniMeal, Founders Fish Fertilizer, Boost & Bloom.
Sun & zone (helps you choose the right plants)
Full sun: 6+ hours of direct sun per day.
Partial shade: about 4+ hours; more shade tolerant.
Hardiness zone: your climate rating. You can set this at the top of the website so you only see plants that can survive your winters.

Do you have a sunny spot, a more shady spot, or a mix?

turns.replyText:
How do I use it properly the very first time?

Great question – using it right the first time sets you up really well. I’ll keep this super simple for the Get Growing Bundle.

If you are planting in the ground

Dig the hole

About 2 feet wide and 2 feet deep.

Cow manure

Put a few inches of your regular soil in the bottom of the hole.
Mix some aged cow manure into the soil you removed and use that mix to start filling back in around the rose.

Bone meal

Mix about 1 cup of bone meal into that soil/manure mix around the roots as you plant.

Mint compost

After the rose is planted, spread mint compost on top of the soil around the base of the plant like a mulch (a thin blanket).
Keep it a couple inches away from the main stem.

Founders Fish Fertilizer

Mix 4 oz per gallon of water.
Water the rose with this mix right after planting.
Then use it again every 4–6 weeks during the growing season.
If you are planting in a container

Potting mix + cow manure

In a large pot with drainage, mix cow manure into your potting soil before you plant.
Fill the pot with this mix and plant the rose so it sits at the same level it was in its nursery pot.

Bone meal

Mix about 1 cup of bone meal into that potting mix when you plant.

Mint compost (top layer)

After planting, spread mint compost on top of the soil around the rose as a mulch.

Founders Fish Fertilizer

Mix 4 oz per gallon of water.
Water with this right after planting.
Then use it every 3–4 weeks during the growing season.

If you tell me whether your rose is going in the ground or a pot, and roughly how big the pot is if you’re container planting, I can fine-tune these steps just for your setup.
